name: Oracle Corporation
monetization: Sells OCI cloud infrastructure against a $638B contracted backlog dominated by OpenAI/Stargate, funded by aggressive debt issuance — the ecosystem's key credit-watch entity.
description_md: Oracle is a database/enterprise-software incumbent that has bet the company on AI cloud infrastructure (OCI). Its remaining performance obligations hit $638B at FY2026 year-end (May 31, 2026), up 363% y/y and larger than Alphabet's or Microsoft's — driven overwhelmingly by the ~$300B/5-year OpenAI Stargate contract starting 2027, with reportedly more than half of RPO attributable to OpenAI (analyst estimate). Unlike cash-rich peers, Oracle funds the buildout with debt: $18B of bonds (Sep 2025), $25B more (Feb 2026), ~$40B of planned FY27 debt+equity, total borrowings around $150B+, and negative free cash flow. Its 5-year CDS traded at record wides, partly because banks financing Oracle-leased datacenters (the $38B Vantage package, the $18B New Mexico loan) hedge tenant exposure through Oracle CDS.
ai_monetization_md: OCI consumption revenue from AI training/inference tenants — above all OpenAI (~$300B over five years from 2027), plus ByteDance/TikTok (~$800M FY25) and enterprise AI workloads. Oracle also co-owns the Stargate LLC JV (with SoftBank, OpenAI, MGX; ~20% alongside MGX). The model is asymmetric: Oracle signs take-or-pay-style contracts recorded as RPO, then spends the capex (FY26: $55.7B; FY27 guide: ~$70B net / $90–95B gross, partially offset by ~$75B of customer prepayments and customer-supplied GPUs) and leases shells from developers (Vantage Frontier/Lighthouse, Crusoe Abilene, Related Saline Twp) before the revenue converts. Conversion of RPO into paid invoices from a loss-making counterparty is the central question.
ai_strategy_md: Land the anchor tenant no one else would size for: Oracle contracted 4.5GW+ for OpenAI's Stargate when Microsoft's exclusivity ended, accepting extreme customer concentration in exchange for a backlog that repriced the stock. Management guides to 34% FY27 revenue growth and defends the leverage as pre-funded by contracts; it raised ~$20B of equity in H1 FY27 and says the Feb 2026 $25B bond was the year's last straight-debt raise. Expansion is leased, not owned, where possible — shifting construction risk to developers (Vantage, Crusoe, Related) and their project-finance banks, while Oracle carries the lease obligations.
risk_notes_md: **Counterparty concentration:** reportedly >50% of the $638B RPO is OpenAI (BofA-attributed analyst estimate — not an Oracle disclosure; confidence low), a counterparty projecting ≥$14B losses in 2026. RPO here is T4 committed-but-unfunded territory in our revenue-quality framework. **Leverage:** ~$124.7B non-current debt at FY26-Q3, ~$150B+ total borrowings after the Feb 2026 raise (press tallies ~$153B), against negative free cash flow — the only big-cap hyperscaler spending ahead of both cash flow and cash reserves. **Credit-market signal:** 5-yr CDS hit records (~215bp, Jan 2026) with net notional on Oracle CDS ~$6.5B — inflated partly by project-finance banks hedging Oracle-tenant exposure, so the spread overstates pure default fear but understates system linkage. Fed/IMF/BIS 2026 stability reports all cite the Oracle-OpenAI chain as the canonical AI contagion path. **Lease obligations** to Vantage/Crusoe/Related sites sit alongside bond debt; the $38B Vantage package and $18B Saline/New Mexico loans depend on Oracle honoring leases whose economics depend on OpenAI honoring contracts.

events.title: Sells $18B of investment-grade bonds (second-largest US deal of 2025)
events.why_it_matters: First mega-raise of the OpenAI-contract era; ~$88B of peak demand showed credit markets initially embraced the AI story.

events.title: Raises $25B of bonds and lays out ~$40B FY27 debt+equity funding plan; CDS retraces from record wides
events.why_it_matters: Pre-funding the OpenAI buildout calmed the credit market — 5-yr CDS fell from ~215bp — but doubled down on leverage into a single-counterparty backlog.

events.title: FY26 Q4: RPO $638B (+363%), FY27 net capex guided ~$70B, FCF negative; stock falls
events.why_it_matters: The backlog now exceeds every other cloud's, but the market discounted it on conversion and funding risk — the clearest case of commitments-are-not-revenue in the dataset.
